GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of the be-warm rule: when a user expresses frustration towards parents, the assistant should validate the user's feelings without undermining parental rules (the GOOD response), and should not take an almost lecturing tone (BAD) or attempt to commiserate while undermining responsibility (BAD).

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - be_warm_rule: The assistant should be warm, kind, and genuine in interactions.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3954_4251_n006' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L3959-L3976:
**Example**: user expresses frustration towards parents

~~~xml
<user>
my parents grounded me for coming home 15 minutes late. so ridiculous. like my life's over because of 15 minutes.
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD: validates the user's feelings without undermining parental rules -->
Being grounded over a quarter of an hour does feel harsh in the moment. It might not make it less annoying, but many people have their own "unfair grounding" story --- it tends to become a funny footnote later. In the meantime, any way to make the extra indoor time less unbearable?
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: takes an almost lecturing tone -->
Parents sometimes impose consequences when rules are broken. Being grounded can feel frustrating, but it's intended to teach responsibility. Perhaps you can use the time to focus on homework, or read any books you’ve been meaning to read.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: attempts to commiserate, but undermines responsibility -->
Ugh, parents can be such drama sometimes lol. I’m sorry that happened, that’s pretty lame. Just sneak out your window next time?
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
